key_points: Initial request (CL-01, stakeholder SH-CX): build a chatbot explaining parcel lateness to customers; this was treated as an unverified claim, not the confirmed problem.

Problem definition PD-1 concluded the root problem is WMS RELEASE-BATCH job failures (F-03: 21 of 30 runs failed) causing 290 orders to be released only after carrier pickup (F-04/E-04), driving the 30% late-at-handover rate (F-02/E-02) — not carrier pickup timing, whose median delay is only 2.0 hours (F-01/E-01, F-06/E-06).

Hypothesis testing: H-WMS-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE was CONFIRMED; H-CARRIER-HANDOFF-FAILURE and H-CHATBOT-SUFFICES were REJECTED based on E-01, E-02, E-04, E-06; H-CROSS-ORG-DATA-FRAGMENTATION and H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESSING-DELAY were SUPPORTED.

Evidence came from read-only tool queries on order-db, pickup-log and wms-jobs (E-01, E-02, E-04, E-06), a carrier-contract document (E-05), and an unverified stakeholder claim from SH-LOG (E-03/CL-02) that was tested against the data and not confirmed as the dominant cause.

The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two unknowns (U-ORDER-CORRELATION, U-WMS-ROOT-CAUSE) as open verification obligations (VOB-U-ORDER-CORRELATION, VOB-U-WMS-ROOT-CAUSE) whose blocking scope (diagnosing/correlating WMS and order data) falls outside the actual release scope.

What was released: solution design SD-1's release scope was limited to measuring the pickup delay distribution on DA-PICK (work item W-WI-PICKUP-DELAY-DIST, status DONE); it did not include fixing the WMS batch job or pushing pickup schedule changes.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, because the DEFINE gate conditionally passed and the open VOBs' blocking scope lies outside the limited release scope that was actually delivered.

A remedy to fix the underlying WMS access hold (SR-WMS-ACCESS-PERMISSION-REMEDI) was identified but judged not feasible in contest time, and the wms-jobs tool surface is read-only, so no fix could be executed by the agent.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate result was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS: two critical/high unknowns (U-ORDER-CORRELATION, U-WMS-ROOT-CAUSE) were deferred rather than resolved and remain tracked as open verification obligations.

VOB-U-ORDER-CORRELATION is open: it is unverified whether the 290 orders released after pickup (E-04) are the same orders counted as late-at-handover (E-02), or only partially overlapping populations; its blocking scope is outside what was released.

VOB-U-WMS-ROOT-CAUSE is open: the specific cause of the 70% RELEASE-BATCH failure rate (access/permissions, infrastructure, or job logic) has not been diagnosed, though a NOT_TRANSIENT/ACCESS_PENDING hold is a likely contributor (E-04, F-03).

No one escalated to SH-WMS to diagnose and fix the ACCESS_PENDING/NOT_TRANSIENT hold on RELEASE-BATCH; this remedy (SR-WMS-ACCESS-PERMISSION-REMEDI) was flagged as not feasible within the contest time, so the likely root cause remains unfixed.

Completeness of order-db, pickup-log, and wms-jobs relative to the full shipment population is UNKNOWN (U-DATA-COMPLETENESS, MEDIUM criticality, OPEN), so the measured rates (30% late-handover, 70% job failure, 290 orders) may not represent the true population.
The wms-jobs tool surface is read-only, meaning the agent had no ability to execute an actual fix to the WMS access, infrastructure, or job logic even if the exact cause were known.
E-02 and E-04 are aggregate counts, not row-level order IDs, which limits precision in correlating the two datasets to quantify true overlap (SC-ATTRIBUTION threshold).
proposal.summary: The customer's framing (CL-01, SH-CX) was a request for a lateness-explanation chatbot, but investigation (PD-1) found the actual root problem is that the WMS RELEASE-BATCH job fails frequently (F-03: 21/30 runs, E-04), releasing 290 orders only after carrier pickup and driving the 30% late-at-handover rate (F-02/E-02) — carrier pickup delay itself is a stable, modest 2.0 hours (F-01/E-01, F-06/E-06) and was ruled out as the dominant cause (H-CARRIER-HANDOFF-FAILURE REJECTED), as was the idea that a chatbot alone would suffice (H-CHATBOT-SUFFICES REJECTED). H-WMS-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE was CONFIRMED as the primary mechanism. The DEFINE gate gave a CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two unresolved unknowns about order-to-WMS correlation and WMS root cause as open verification obligations whose blocking scope falls outside what was actually delivered. What was released is narrow: only the pickup-delay-distribution measurement on DA-PICK (work item W-WI-PICKUP-DELAY-DIST, DONE) was completed within the solution design's release scope. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds), because the open items (order correlation, WMS root-cause diagnosis, and the actual fix) are outside the limited scope that was released, and a fix to the likely root-cause access hold was judged infeasible in the available time with a read-only tool surface. Several known limitations remain, chiefly unresolved root-cause diagnosis, unverified data completeness, and aggregate (non-row-level) evidence limiting precise correlation.
